nav.label: Commercial sections
license.readOnly: Your company's license doesn't include Commercial right now. You can view bids and the library, but not change them.
library.title: Library
library.subtitle: Unit costs, labor rates and the templates that turn direct cost into a selling price.
error.noCompany: Your user isn't linked to a company.
field.name: Name
prices.errCost: Enter a unit cost of zero or more.
prices.confirmDelete: Delete this price? Estimates already priced keep their values.
prices.linked: Linked to the RitsuScope material catalog: recipes using this product get this price.
prices.notLinked: Not in the RitsuScope catalog: matched by name and unit.
prices.empty: No prices yet for this country. Add the products your recipes use.
prices.footnote: To change a price, add a new one with its valid-from date. Old estimates keep the price they were made with.
labor.errNumbers: Rate and burden must be zero or more.
labor.errDuplicate: This trade already has a rate starting on that date.
labor.empty: No labor rates yet for this country.
labor.footnote: Burden is encargos sociais in Brazil and labor burden (payroll taxes, insurance, benefits) in the USA. Recipes point at a trade by its code.
templates.errRate: Rates must be numbers of zero or more.
templates.errTaxes: Taxes on the price add up to 100% or more.
templates.errDuplicate: There is already a template with this name, or another default for this country.
templates.confirmDelete: Delete this template? Bids that use it keep their own copy of the lines.
templates.noneYet: None yet. Copy a standard template to start.
templates.standardNote: Standard templates come with 0% rates. Copy this one to your company and set your own rates.
templates.makeDefault: Default for new bids in this country
templates.rulesNote: Percent lines run in order and add to the running subtotal. Divisor lines are taxes on the selling price: they are summed and applied last, price = subtotal ÷ (1 − taxes).
templates.pick: Pick a template on the left, or create a new one.
newBid.title: New bid
newBid.subtitle: Takeoff, pricing and proposal. It won't use an active-project slot.
newBid.name: Job name
newBid.noTemplate: No template for this country (price = direct cost)
newBid.later: Address, contract, billing and schedule are asked only if the bid is won and converted to a project.
bids.title: Bids
bids.subtitle: Every bid your company is pricing, submitted, won or lost.
bids.search: Search job, client or bid number
bids.emptyFirst: No bids yet. Create the first one to start a takeoff and estimate.
bid.notePrompt: Add a short note (who won, why, next steps). Optional.
bid.notFound: Bid not found, or you don't have access to it.
takeoff.title: Takeoff in RitsuScope
takeoff.hint: Quantities come from RitsuScope. After changing the takeoff, refresh the estimate.
estimate.unpricedCount: {count} items have products or trades without a price in the library.
estimate.noRecipe: {count} takeoff items have no recipe in RitsuScope, so they have quantity but no cost.
estimate.uncalibrated: {count} sheets have no scale and were skipped.
estimate.noTakeoff: No takeoff items found yet: open the Takeoff tab to measure in RitsuScope.
estimate.confirmRemove: Remove this item from the estimate?
estimate.confirmIssue: Issue this revision? It will be frozen; later changes go into a new revision.
estimate.revised: New revision created from the issued one.
estimate.frozen: This revision was issued and is frozen. Create a new revision to change it.
estimate.empty: No items yet. Refresh from takeoff, or add items by hand.
estimate.detail.missingHint: Add these to the price book or labor rates, then refresh from takeoff.
estimate.footnote: Takeoff items are priced from their RitsuScope recipe (materials and labor lines) and the library, valid on the revision's pricing date. Unit costs can be adjusted by hand.
estimate.noLines: No add-on lines: the price equals the direct cost.
proposal.exportedDraft: PDF downloaded. This revision is still a draft: issue it in the Estimate tab once the client has it, so the numbers sent are frozen.
proposal.draftNote: Write the proposal before issuing the revision: once issued, its text is frozen with the numbers.
proposal.scopeHint: What the price covers, in a few sentences.
proposal.paymentTermsHint: E.g. 30% on mobilization, balance by monthly progress
proposal.notesHint: Anything else the client should know
pdf.title: Commercial proposal
pdf.unitPriceNote: Unit prices include indirect costs, taxes and profit.
convert.title: Convert to project
convert.notIssued: No revision was issued, so the latest draft becomes the baseline. Issue it first if the client received a different version.
convert.carriedTakeoff: Takeoff: {sheets} sheets, {items} items, levels and zones
convert.carriedEstimate: Every estimate revision, with the baseline marked
convert.toFill: Still to fill in the project form
convert.toFillList: Address, billing method and cycle, retainage, start date and contractual term.
convert.floors: Create {count} Floor locations from the RitsuScope levels (Location Breakdown)
convert.counts: After converting, the job counts toward active projects once its status is Active.
attach.title: Attachments
attach.hint: Checked PDFs are added after the proposal pages, in one file.
attach.howTo: To update the takeoff drawings, open the Takeoff tab and print again in RitsuScope: the newest export replaces the previous one here.
import.missingColumns: The file needs these columns: {columns}. Download the template to see the layout.
import.col.name: Name
import.summary: {ok} prices ready to import · {bad} lines with problems (skipped)
import.reason.name: no name
import.reason.cost: unit cost missing or not a number
import.reason.date: date not understood (use dd/mm/yyyy or yyyy-mm-dd)
import.note: Each line is added as a new price. Products with the same name and unit as a RitsuScope catalog material are linked to it. Lines without a date are valid from today.
import.done: {count} prices imported ({linked} linked to the RitsuScope catalog).
templates.setNote: Mark lines as "Material BDI" to price materials with their own, lower BDI (BDI diferenciado). The other lines then apply to labor, equipment and subcontracts only.
abc.title: ABC curve
abc.empty: No priced items yet. Refresh the estimate from the takeoff first.
abc.note.inputs: Inputs are summed across all items from each item's priced detail. Costs typed by hand stay with their item. Class A = the lines that make up the first 80% of the direct cost, B = up to 95%, C = the rest.
abc.note.items: Each estimate item at its full direct cost (material + labor + equipment + subcontract). Class A = the items that make up the first 80% of the direct cost, B = up to 95%, C = the rest.
calendar.noDate: {count} open bids have no due date
insights.markupWon: Average BDI / markup of won bids
insights.markupLost: Average BDI / markup of lost bids
insights.readHigher: Lost bids carried {diff} more markup on average: price may be part of why they were lost.
insights.readNotPrice: Lost bids did not carry more markup than won ones: look beyond price (scope, deadline, relationship).
insights.note: Win rate = won ÷ (won + lost); declined and open bids don't count. Markup = latest revision's selling price ÷ direct cost − 1. Clients are grouped by name.
insights.reasonsTitle: Why bids are lost or declined
actuals.noBaseline: This project has no estimate revision to compare with.
actuals.baseline: Compared with the contract baseline: {name}. Actuals come from FieldOp: check-in/out hours, daily report production and materials received.
actuals.noData: FieldOp has no hours or daily reports for this project yet.
actuals.progressHint: Weighted by direct cost, items that report production
actuals.productivityGood: Crews produce at or above the estimate
actuals.productivityBad: Crews need more hours than estimated
actuals.unlinked: {count} items have no FieldOp activity linked (RitsuScope item → Scope Allocation), so their progress is unknown.
actuals.note: Earned value = each line's baseline direct cost × its progress. Earned hours = estimated hours × progress; the productivity index divides them by the hours worked in FieldOp. Alternates are left out. Materials are matched by name and unit.
estimate.kind.label: Line kind
estimate.kind.alternateHint: Alternate: priced, but not included in the bid price.
estimate.alternatesHint: Each alternate is priced with this revision's BDI / markup and listed apart on the proposal.
pdf.allowancesNote: Allowances are included in the total price and adjusted to the actual amount spent.
pdf.alternatesNote: Alternates are not included in the total price; each one is added only if accepted.
clauses.confirmRemove: Delete this clause? Proposals that already use it keep their text.
clauses.hint: Ready-made lines for proposals. In a bid's Proposal tab, pick them from "Insert from library"; conditions go into Notes.
clauses.empty: No clauses of this kind yet.
costs.title: Actual costs
costs.confirmUndo: Delete the {count} entries of the last import?
costs.unmatched: {count} entries name an estimate line that doesn't exist; they will be imported without a line.
costs.cpiGood: At or under budget for the work done
costs.cpiBad: Over budget for the work done
costs.cvHint: Earned value − actual cost; negative = overrun
costs.empty: No actual costs yet. Add them one by one or import a CSV from your ERP or spreadsheet.
costs.unlinkedNote: {amount} of actual cost is not linked to an estimate line: it counts in the totals and categories, not per line.
